diagnosis.what_happened: Naive length filtering of bibliographic references caused subheading and non-reference text leakage into the master thesis bibliography.
diagnosis.behavior_caused_outcome: Character-length-only heuristics (VIOLATED_ASSUMPTION_IGNORED) misidentified long subheadings and regular text blocks as bibliography entries.
diagnosis.what_should_have_happened: Reference parsing should rely on structural markers, such as standard APA 7 formatting rules, regex matching of years/DOIs, or scholarly metadata rather than simple string length.
diagnosis.rationale_why: Bibliographies are highly structured artifacts; relying on raw string length introduces severe false positives.

desired_behavior: When extracting or parsing references, always employ structural validation (e.g., matching authors, years, DOIs, or using specialized reference extraction libraries) and explicitly forbid naive character-length filtering.
generalization: Parsing structured academic elements requires semantic or structural heuristics, never raw textual dimensions.
